title: Breach Predictor AI Assist dashboard and its AI agents

prose.text: {{threat-summary}} Licensing and the Triage verdict scale are open {{gap:availability-and-verdicts}}.

access.statement: The AI Assist feature's access is to be asked of the Zscaler Account team, and AI Assist can be opened from any screen in the portal.

quotes: To learn more about getting access to this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
On any screen in the Breach Predictor Portal, you can click AI Assist to open the dashboard

availability.statement: The June 30, 2025 release summary lists the AI Assist Dashboard as a Feature in Limited Availability.

inputs.statement: The AI Assist dashboard is powered by multiple Breach Predictor AI agents and draws on log sources, peer best practices, current policy settings, third-party integrations and ThreatLabz threat data.

quotes: Powered by multiple Breach Predictor AI agents
multiple log sources, peer best practices, current policy settings, third-party integrations, and cutting-edge threat data from Zscaler ThreatLabz

agents.statement: The AI Assist dashboard lists five agents: Detection (detects threats), Context (provides additional details about specific threats), Triage (gives an initial verdict and confidence level for each threat), Response (responds to each threat and provides next steps) and Third-Party Integrations (monitors the integrated third-party applications).

quotes: At the top of the AI Assist dashboard, you see the status of the Breach AI Agents that are actively monitoring and analyzing threats across your organization:
Detection: This agent detects threats across your organization.
Context: This agent provides additional details about specific threats (e.g., affected users, assets, etc.).
Triage: This agent triages the threats in your organization to provide an initial verdict and confidence level for each threat.
Response: This agent responds to each threat, and provides next steps to address threats.
Third-Party Integrations: This agent monitors the third-party applications you've integrated with Breach Predictor

prompts.statement: Each AI Assist page offers suggested prompts that change dynamically with the current screen and the primary agent engaged, or a text box for own questions; thumbs up and thumbs down feedback is available.

quotes: The prompts change dynamically based on the current screen you're viewing and the primary AI agent being engaged.
On each of the pages in the AI Assist dashboard, you can click one of the suggested prompts to get more information, or you can enter your own question in the text box.
You can also provide feedback (i.e., thumbs up and thumbs down)

top-response.statement: On the AI Assist dashboard, the Top Response Actions tile gives a prioritized list of recommended policy updates from the Response Agent.

quotes: you can click the Top Response Actions tile to see a prioritized list of recommended policy updates from the Response Agent.

threat-summary.statement: On the Attack path tab, clicking AI Assist gives generative AI information about the threat; the threat summary has general ThreatLabz information and Breach Predictor's analysis of the threats at each attack stage, including the log source.

quotes: Click AI Assist to see generative AI information about the threat

The threat summary includes general information from Zscaler ThreatLabz, as well as specific information from Breach Predictor's analysis of the threats posed at each attack stage, including the log source for the threat data.

availability-and-verdicts.title: AI Assist licence or edition requirements, whether it remains in limited availability, and the Triage agent's verdict scale
availability-and-verdicts.detail: The June 30, 2025 release summary lists AI Assist as Limited Availability and the articles point to the Zscaler Account team for access, but give no licence or edition requirement, no later availability status, and no scale for the Triage agent's initial verdict and confidence level.
